workflow.title: Understand reading and attention concerns
workflow.question: What do the current assessment records establish about this child’s reading and attention difficulties, and what still needs assessment?
workflow.description: A fictional record-review example, not a diagnostic instrument. The finite catalogue describes possible professionally recorded reading and attention assessment conclusions, including coexistence and uncharacterized concerns. It is not an exhaustive catalogue of causes of poor grades. Only explicitly accepted, current records for the declared child, assessment episode and context constrain those possibilities. Logical agreement does not authenticate a record, establish clinical validity, attribute the cause of grades, prescribe support or estimate diagnostic probabilities.

assumptions: All people, records, observations and assessment conclusions in this example are fictional. No scores, diagnostic thresholds or treatment-effect estimates are supplied.
A poor grade, unfinished work or a reading concern excludes no possibility. A concern is not a professional assessment conclusion.

No compatible interpretation means these submitted records and fixed rules cannot be reconciled. It does not establish that the child has no difficulty or has no diagnosis.
No probability, causal attribution, diagnostic validity, clinical prescription or support-plan benefit is inferred from interpretation counts or logical agreement.

case.title: Fictional reading and attention assessment records for Sam, age eight
case.scope: Sam is a fictional eight-year-old with poor grades and reported classroom difficulties. Lisa coordinates a review of what the current professional assessment records establish. Neither dyslexia nor ADHD is assumed in the opening case. Grades are a reason to investigate, not a diagnostic test. Both conditions, neither condition and explanations outside this limited catalogue remain possible. No clinical recommendation or individual diagnosis is generated.

actions.label: Request qualified assessment of the unresolved reading concern

value.summary: Check whether a qualified professional has already assessed the reading concern. Obtain the applicable record or ask that professional what further assessment is appropriate. Poor grades alone establish no reading diagnosis.

actions.label: Request qualified assessment of the unresolved attention concern

value.summary: Obtain any current applicable professional attention-assessment record, or ask a qualified professional what assessment is appropriate. A reading finding does not settle ADHD or the cause of classroom difficulties.

actions.label: Discuss support for the professionally recorded reading need

value.summary: Discuss appropriate support with the child, family and qualified professionals while any unresolved attention assessment proceeds. This record review does not prescribe an intervention or predict individual benefit; use a separate support comparison only with explicitly supplied outcome assumptions.
